# Implementation Plan: RBAC Authentication & Authorization

**Branch**: `001-rbac-auth` | **Date**: 2026-08-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-rbac-auth/spec.md`

**Note**: This file is generated by `/speckit-plan`; the artifact definitions below drive the implementation.

## Summary

Add server-side authentication and RBAC authorization to zelo. Users register only via a
syndic-issued invitation that identifies their condominium, unit, and invited role
(`owner` or `tenant`). They sign in with email + password, and the system enforces access
by role. The `syndic` role can only be granted by the current syndic to a user who
currently holds the `owner` role; `tenant` users are never eligible. Sessions are
server-side: the browser receives only a session ID in an HTTP cookie, and session data
lives in PostgreSQL. A `docker-compose.yml` provides a local PostgreSQL container.

Technical direction for this feature: **standard library first** (no web frameworks, no
ORM, no migration framework) and **CSS-first over JavaScript**, while keeping the
constitution-mandated GOTTH presentation stack (Templ, Tailwind CSS, HTMX).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Go 1.27 (module `github.com/leoarkiteto/zelo`), using the Go
standard library as the primary toolset.

**Primary Dependencies**:
- `github.com/a-h/templ` — server-rendered templates (constitution-mandated)
- Tailwind CSS + HTMX — CSS-first styling and minimal progressive enhancement
  (constitution-mandated)
- `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib` — PostgreSQL driver registered with stdlib
  `database/sql` (driver only; no ORM)
- `golang.org/x/crypto` — Argon2id password hashing (official Go extension; stdlib has
  no safe password-hashing primitive)

**Storage**: PostgreSQL (local `docker-compose.yml` container) accessed via
`database/sql` + `pgx` stdlib driver and plain SQL; tables: `users`, `condominiums`,
`units`, `unit_occupancies`, `user_roles`, `invitations`, `sessions`, `audit_events`.

**Testing**: stdlib only — `testing`, `net/http/httptest`, and integration tests against
the dockerized PostgreSQL. No assertion or mocking frameworks.

**Target Platform**: Linux server (server-rendered web application).

**Project Type**: web application (server-side GOTTH stack; no client-side SPA).

**Performance Goals**: Auth pages and role-restricted pages respond in under 2 seconds
for a typical condominium (hundreds of users); sign-in/registration complete in under 2
minutes of user time.

**Constraints**:
- Standard library first: no web framework, no ORM, no session/migration/CSRF frameworks.
- CSS-first over JavaScript: prefer CSS for presentation and interaction; HTMX is used
  only for server-driven partial updates required by the GOTTH stack.
- Session cookie is `HttpOnly`, `Secure` (in production), `SameSite=Lax`.
- Passwords never stored in plaintext; Argon2id hashing.
- CSRF protection on all state-changing routes (custom synchronizer-token middleware).
- Migrations are plain forward-only SQL files applied by a minimal runner.
- No client-side SPA framework.

**Scale/Scope**: Hundreds of users per deployment; 3 roles (`syndic`, `owner`, `tenant`);
one condominium per user account for v1.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| I. GOTTH Stack | PASS | Go server + Templ + Tailwind + HTMX; no SPA. User's "no frameworks" constraint is applied to Go/web infrastructure, not to the constitution-mandated presentation stack. CSS-first aligns with Tailwind. |
| II. Modular Monolith with Hexagonal Architecture | PASS | Use cases in `internal/service` depend only on stdlib interfaces; adapters in `internal/store`, `internal/auth`, `internal/handler`; shared models in `internal/model`. |
| III. Vertical Slice Feature Isolation | PASS | Auth slice spans `handler → service → store` only; shared code restricted to `internal/model`, `internal/middleware`, `internal/config`. |
| IV. Test-First Development (NON-NEGOTIABLE) | PASS | Tests written first with stdlib `testing`/`httptest`; integration tests cover sessions, roles, lockout, and migrations. |
| V. SOLID, Design Patterns & Generated Code | PASS | Generated `*_templ.go` and Tailwind output produced only by `scripts/`; no hand edits to generated artifacts. |
| Repository Layout & Conventions | PASS | Follows `README.md` layout; `docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`, `.air.toml`, `.env.example`, `tailwind.config.js` added during implementation. |

**Gate result**: PASS — no violations requiring justification.

**Post-design re-check (after Phase 1)**: Still PASS. The data model keeps RBAC
assignments (`user_roles`) separate from unit relationships (`unit_occupancies`), adds
`invitations` for invite-based registration, and stays implementable with
`database/sql` + plain SQL inside `internal/store`, leaving `internal/service`
framework-free.

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-rbac-auth/
├── plan.md              # This file (/speckit-plan command output)
├── research.md          # Phase 0 output (/speckit-plan command)
├── data-model.md        # Phase 1 output (/speckit-plan command)
├── quickstart.md        # Phase 1 output (/speckit-plan command)
├── contracts/           # Phase 1 output (/speckit-plan command)
└── tasks.md             # Phase 2 output (/speckit-tasks command - NOT created by /speckit-plan)
```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
cmd/web/                  # main entrypoint: wire config → store → service → handler → middleware
internal/
├── auth/                 # custom session manager (crypto/rand + cookie + Postgres),
│                         # Argon2id password hashing, CSRF token middleware
├── config/               # stdlib env config: DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, APP_ENV
├── handler/              # net/http handlers: register, login, logout, password reset, auth guard
├── middleware/           # auth guard, CSRF, request logging, panic recovery, security headers
├── model/                # User, Role, Membership, Invitation, Session, UnitOccupancy
├── service/              # auth use cases: invite, register, authenticate, assign/revoke roles
└── store/                # database/sql + pgx stdlib driver adapters; plain SQL queries
migrations/               # plain forward-only SQL files + minimal migration runner
web/templates/            # Templ sources for auth pages + generated *_templ.go
web/static/               # compiled Tailwind output and vendored HTMX
docker-compose.yml        # local PostgreSQL container
```

**Structure Decision**: Single server-rendered web application. The GOTTH stack renders
HTML on the server; CSS (Tailwind) handles presentation and as much interaction as
possible, with HTMX limited to server-driven partial updates.
